# Generated by `cargo run -p agent_docs` from the diagnostic registry and compiler/tests/ui; do not edit.
title: "V6020 dependency_acquires_authority"
description: "A dependency acquires authority itself: it calls a std host() constructor (Fs.host(), Env.host(), …) or declares an @external binding (RFC 0003 §5.2, experimental)."
---

An error from the `capability` phase. `sakura explain V6020` prints this explanation offline.

A dependency acquires authority itself: it calls a std `host()` constructor (`Fs.host()`,
`Env.host()`, …) or declares an `@external` binding (RFC 0003 §5.2, experimental). In any
package other than the one being built, authority comes only from the consumer: the dependency
performs the effects its public rows declare, through the handlers its caller installs. A
`host()` call reads the program's root grants, so without this rule a dependency could use
`Fs` without `Fs` in any public row. Rewrite the dependency to declare the effect in its row, or,
if you have reviewed it, write `trusted = true` on its line in the consumer's `[dependencies]`;
`sakura audit` and `build --manifest` then list each such site under the package's name. `test`
bodies of a dependency are not compiled by its consumers and are not checked.

Wrong:

```sakura
# util/src/lib.sak, a dependency
import std/env.{Env}
pub fn home() -> Option<String> { with Env.host() { Env.get("HOME") } }
```

Fixed:

```sakura
import std/env.{Env}
pub fn home() -> Option<String> ! {Env} { Env.get("HOME") }
```

## Wrong program

[`compiler/tests/ui/V6020_dependency_external/`](https://github.com/icantcodefyi/sakuralang/blob/main/compiler/tests/ui/V6020_dependency_external/), which the compiler's ui suite runs through `sakura check`:

`main.sak`:

```sakura
// RFC 0003 §5.2: an `@external` declaration in a dependency is `V6020` at the attribute unless the
// root trusts the dependency.
pub fn main() -> Unit ! {Console} { Console.print("hi") }
```

`sakura.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "billing"

[dependencies]
util = { path = "util" }
```
